text:
Some shoppers walk to a farmers' market for tomatoes grown ten kilometres away, while others buy mangoes flown across the world, and opinions differ on whether it is better to buy local produce or imported goods. This essay will consider both views before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of local produce argue that it is fresher and supports farmers. Food grown nearby needs less transport and keeps money in the region. A family that buys vegetables from a farmer in the next village, for example, enjoys produce that was picked yesterday and helps to sustain local jobs. Short journeys mean lower emissions and less packaging, and consumers can learn how their food was grown. Local farms also preserve countryside and traditional varieties, and buying in season encourages a healthy variety of diets. In an emergency, a country with strong local agriculture is less dependent on foreign supply.

On the other hand, supporters of imported goods argue that they offer variety and lower prices. Imported goods supply out-of-season and exotic items often at a lower cost. A shopper in a cold country, for example, can eat fresh fruit in winter and enjoy tea, spices and coffee that cannot grow locally. Specialisation means that some regions can produce food much more efficiently, so that imported produce may even have a smaller carbon footprint than local greenhouse crops. Trade also provides income for farmers in developing countries. However, long supply chains can hide poor labour conditions, and the freshness of imports may be lower. A mix of both suits most households.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that people should buy local produce in season when possible, but they can also enjoy imported goods that cannot be grown nearby.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: mua nông sản địa phương hay hàng nhập khẩu

plan.think: Mở bài tương phản cà chua trồng cách 10 km và xoài bay nửa vòng thế giới; hai phe.

Tươi, hỗ trợ nông dân: ít vận chuyển, giữ tiền trong vùng; ví dụ gia đình mua rau từ nông dân làng bên rau hái hôm qua duy trì việc làm địa phương; chuyến ngắn ít khí thải, bao bì; biết cách trồng; giữ nông thôn, giống truyền thống; mua theo mùa; khủng hoảng ít phụ thuộc nước ngoài.

Đa dạng, giá thấp: hàng trái mùa, lạ giá rẻ; ví dụ người mua ở nước lạnh ăn trái cây tươi mùa đông, trà, gia vị, cà phê không trồng được; chuyên môn hoá hiệu quả hơn, có thể dấu chân carbon thấp hơn nhà kính địa phương; thu nhập cho nông dân nước đang phát triển; nhược: chuỗi cung ứng dài che điều kiện lao động, độ tươi thấp; kết hợp.
Địa phương theo mùa khi có thể, nhập khẩu cho thứ không trồng gần.
